scenes.tts: A mouse lacking the N G F receptor is born with too few sympathetic neurons. Were they never made, or made and then lost?
scenes.visual: Title card: Made, Then Lost. A depleted ganglion with the two question marks from chapter one.
scenes.narration: A mouse lacking the NGF receptor is born with too few sympathetic neurons. Were they never made, or made and then lost?
scenes.caption: A mouse lacking the NGF receptor is born with too few sympathetic neurons. Were they never made, or made and then lost?

scenes.tts: A knockout mouse has a gene disrupted, so it makes no working protein. No antibody is involved.
scenes.visual: A gene diagram with one segment crossed out; no working product from the disrupted gene. Label: knockout.
scenes.narration: A knockout mouse has a gene disrupted, so it makes no working protein. No antibody is involved.

scenes.tts: In nineteen ninety-four, Crowley and colleagues reported mice lacking N G F.
scenes.caption: In 1994, Crowley and colleagues reported mice lacking NGF.
scenes.visual: Credit: Crowley and colleagues, 1994. A mouse schematic labelled NGF-null.
scenes.narration: In 1994, Crowley and colleagues reported mice lacking NGF.

scenes.tts: Smeyne, Klein, Barbacid and colleagues reported mice lacking a working track A, the receptor for N G F.
scenes.caption: Smeyne, Klein, Barbacid and colleagues reported mice lacking a working TrkA, the receptor for NGF.
scenes.visual: Credit: Smeyne, Klein, Barbacid and colleagues, 1994. A receptor in a membrane labelled TrkA, crossed out.
scenes.narration: Smeyne, Klein, Barbacid and colleagues reported mice lacking a working TrkA, the receptor for NGF.

scenes.tts: Both mutants lose sympathetic neurons and many sensory neurons. The antibody doubt is settled.
scenes.visual: An evidence table fills in a row: NGF-null and TrkA-null, sympathetic and sensory neurons lost; tick for genetic necessity.
scenes.narration: Both mutants lose sympathetic neurons and many sensory neurons. The antibody doubt is settled.

scenes.tts: The sensory losses fall on neurons that express track A, mostly small neurons that sense pain and temperature.
scenes.caption: The sensory losses fall on neurons that express TrkA, mostly small neurons that sense pain and temperature.
scenes.visual: Sensory neurons of two sizes; the small TrkA-expressing ones fade. Labels: pain, temperature.
scenes.narration: The sensory losses fall on neurons that express TrkA, mostly small neurons that sense pain and temperature.

scenes.tts: But a count at birth still cannot say whether the neurons were ever made.
scenes.visual: The table row gets a note: made versus lost? not answered.
scenes.narration: But a count at birth still cannot say whether the neurons were ever made.

scenes.tts: In nineteen ninety-six, Anne Fagan, Story Landis, Barbacid and colleagues counted one ganglion at a series of ages.
scenes.caption: In 1996, Anne Fagan, Story Landis, Barbacid and colleagues counted one ganglion at a series of ages.
scenes.visual: Credit: Fagan, Landis, Barbacid and colleagues, 1996.
scenes.narration: In 1996, Anne Fagan, Story Landis, Barbacid and colleagues counted one ganglion at a series of ages.

scenes.tts: It was the superior cervical ganglion, the sympathetic ganglion at the top of the neck.
scenes.visual: A mouse outline with the superior cervical ganglion marked at the top of the neck.
scenes.narration: It was the superior cervical ganglion, the sympathetic ganglion at the top of the neck.

scenes.tts: Here are the axes. Neuron number runs up the side. Embryonic and postnatal age runs along the bottom.
scenes.visual: Empty plot: y axis neuron number, x axis age from embryonic to postnatal. Label: schematic.
scenes.narration: Here are the axes. Neuron number runs up the side. Embryonic and postnatal age runs along the bottom.

scenes.tts: Predict. If track A is needed for survival but not for production, what shape does the mutant curve take?
scenes.caption: Predict. If TrkA is needed for survival but not for production, what shape does the mutant curve take?
scenes.visual: Question card over the empty plot: the TrkA-null curve?
scenes.narration: Predict. If TrkA is needed for survival but not for production, what shape does the mutant curve take?

scenes.tts: Loss of track A did not affect neurogenesis, neuronal markers, or initial axon growth.
scenes.caption: Loss of TrkA did not affect neurogenesis, neuronal markers, or initial axon growth.
scenes.visual: Three ticks: neurogenesis, neuronal markers, initial axon growth, each marked unaffected.
scenes.narration: Loss of TrkA did not affect neurogenesis, neuronal markers, or initial axon growth.

scenes.tts: In this schematic, the two counts match at embryonic day thirteen and a half, soon after the ganglion forms.
scenes.visual: Two curves, normal and TrkA-null, together at embryonic day 13.5. Label: schematic, not data.
scenes.narration: In this schematic, the two counts match at embryonic day 13.5, soon after the ganglion forms.
scenes.caption: In this schematic, the two counts match at embryonic day 13.5, soon after the ganglion forms.

scenes.tts: By embryonic day fifteen and a half, the mutant ganglion already has fewer neurons. The gap keeps growing.
scenes.caption: By embryonic day 15.5, the mutant ganglion already has fewer neurons. The gap keeps growing.
scenes.visual: By embryonic day 15.5 the TrkA-null curve sits a little below the normal curve, and the gap widens at later ages. Label: schematic, not data.
scenes.narration: By embryonic day 15.5, the mutant ganglion already has fewer neurons. The gap keeps growing.

scenes.tts: The ganglion formed, and then lost its neurons. The neurons were produced. What failed was survival.
scenes.visual: Caption: produced, then lost. What failed was survival.
scenes.narration: The ganglion formed, and then lost its neurons. The neurons were produced. What failed was survival.

scenes.tts: This time course is the signature evidence that the loss is a failure of survival, not production.
scenes.visual: Three small icons beside a single late count: too few precursors, failed differentiation, excess death.
scenes.narration: This time course is the signature evidence that the loss is a failure of survival, not production.

scenes.tts: Counts of dividing and dying cells showed why. More neurons were dying, and division was normal.
scenes.visual: The two curves again, with dying nuclei counted in the mutant ganglion; the icons for precursors and differentiation fade, leaving excess death.
scenes.narration: Counts of dividing and dying cells showed why. More neurons were dying, and division was normal.

scenes.tts: How does N G F hold off that death? Neurons that get too little die by a death that needs the protein Bax.
scenes.caption: How does NGF hold off that death? Neurons that get too little die by a death that needs the protein Bax.
scenes.visual: A neuron with a death program labelled Bax; NGF signalling holds a brake on it.
scenes.narration: How does NGF hold off that death? Neurons that get too little die by a death that needs the protein Bax.

scenes.tts: Mice lacking Bax keep sympathetic neurons that would otherwise die. In culture, they survive when N G F is withdrawn.
scenes.visual: The evidence table adds a row: Bax-null, sympathetic neurons kept; in a culture dish, Bax-null neurons survive NGF withdrawal.
scenes.narration: Mice lacking Bax keep sympathetic neurons that would otherwise die. In culture, they survive when NGF is withdrawn.
scenes.caption: Mice lacking Bax keep sympathetic neurons that would otherwise die. In culture, they survive when NGF is withdrawn.

scenes.tts: So N G F works by holding back a Bax dependent death program.
scenes.caption: So NGF works by holding back a Bax dependent death program.
scenes.visual: The brake image again, labelled: NGF holds back a Bax-dependent death program.
scenes.narration: So NGF works by holding back a Bax dependent death program.

scenes.tts: Takeaway: without track A, sympathetic neurons are made and then lost. N G F acts as a survival factor.
scenes.caption: Takeaway: without TrkA, sympathetic neurons are made and then lost. NGF acts as a survival factor.
scenes.visual: Closing card: made, then lost. NGF is a survival factor. The checklist item remove factor, more die, is ticked.
scenes.narration: Takeaway: without TrkA, sympathetic neurons are made and then lost. NGF acts as a survival factor.
